headline: IRL Clash uses AI to get you outside for photo battles
summary: This new app matches players based on location for real-world photography challenges, judged by AI.
details: IRL Clash is a new real-world multiplayer photography game that uses AI to get players outdoors. Players enter a nickname and share their location, and when two active players are close enough, they are matched into a battle.

Each battle consists of five rounds, with players receiving random outdoor photography missions like 'Find an interesting leaf' or 'Capture an unusual tree'. Players can use their phone's camera or select a photo from their gallery.

After the fifth round, an AI referee evaluates the submitted images, providing a score out of 100 and an explanation. The scores are combined to determine the winner, making it a playful reason for friends, students, or meetups to engage with the outdoors.

The application is built as a full-stack project with a React + Vite frontend and a Java 21 Spring Boot backend. It utilizes browser geolocation and camera APIs for a seamless mobile experience. Notably, this version keeps all data in memory, intentionally omitting a database for a lightweight demo.

The developers emphasize that the AI's role is to evaluate outdoor finds, not to increase screen time. Future versions could explore open-weight multimodal models and local inference for enhanced privacy and flexibility, potentially allowing the AI referee to run on edge devices.
The project was developed with AI-assisted tools for architecture, debugging, and deployment. It is currently deployed on Render, with the backend exposing multiplayer game APIs.

The application is built as a full-stack project with a React + Vite frontend and a Java 21 Spring Boot backend. It utilizes browser geolocation and camera APIs for a seamless mobile experience. Notably, this version keeps all data in memory, intentionally omitting a database for a lightweight demo.
